verdict.rationale: The vendor documents building blocks for an assistant you can delegate to: a voice agent session that listens, thinks and answers (docs-26), and SDK-owned tool call-and-execute loops (docs-1). The rcli voice assistant is the closest thing to a built-in delegating assistant, but hands-on reports contradict it working. A user's 'navigate to google.com in safari' command did nothing while the assistant claimed success (comm-4, comm-7), and the vendor acknowledged small models confuse intent with execution (comm-8). Other users hit segfaults and failed installs (comm-3, comm-14). Missing for 10: first-party documentation of a built-in assistant that executes delegated tasks, reliable grounding of tool actions, and independent confirmation that delegated tasks actually complete.
